 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a road traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 02.09.2016 at about 5.00 a.m., in front of Maderahalli Plantation situated on Chennai - Bengaluru (NH75) road, Kolar, Mr. Sagar @
Sagar Gowda (hereinafter referred as deceased) who was travelling as an occupant in a Ford Icon car bearing Reg.No.KA05MD9550 sustained grievous injuries on account of the actionable negligence of the driver of the said vehicle (respondent No.1).
Immediately thereafter he was being rushed to R.L.Jalappa Hospital, Kolar.
Unfortunately on the way to the hospital the deceased succumbed to the fatal injuries.
Postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies by spending substantial amount.
As the accident was caused due to the negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA05MD9550 the respondents are jointly & severally liable to pay compensation.
3. The respondent No.1 filed written statement denying the petition averments in toto.

He specifically contended that at the time of the accident the car was being driven by the deceased whereas he and his brother Mr. Kishore Kumar were seated in the front and rear seat of the said car respectively.
The deceased who was not wearing seat belt at the time of the accident sustained injuries on account of his own negligence.
Alleging that a false case is registered against him by the jurisdictional police, prayed for dismissal of the petition as against him.

4. The respondent No.2 filed a separate written statement wherein he contended that on 28.05.2014 he had transferred the ownership of car bearing Reg.No.KA05MD9550 to one Mr.Shaiju for a sum of Rs.90,000/.
Subsequent to such transfer of ownership and delivery of car to Mr. Shaiju he was under a bonafide belief that said Shaiju would have got changed the RC of the car to his name.
Anyhow after the sale of the car he had no control over it.
Hence the first respondent who was having control over the vehicle as on the date of accident and who was also responsible for causing the accident is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Stating so, prayed for dismissal of the petition against him.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 02.09.2016 at about 5.00 a.m.,
in front of Maderahalli Plantation situated on Chennai - ) Sri. Ramakrishne Gowda.

Bengaluru (NH75) road, Kolar
due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Ford Icon car bearing Reg.No.KA05MD9550 ?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ?

If so what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.

What order or award?
6.
The Petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 10 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
Ex. R1
was marked on confrontation during the course of cross examination of PW.1 by respondent No.2.
The respondent No.1 got himself examined as RW.1.
Ex's .R2 to 4 were marked through this witness.
The complainant cum inmate of the car by name Sri.Kishore Kumar was examined as RW.2.

Mr.A.B.Sudhakara s/o A.T.Basavarajaiah, ACP, Vikasasoudha Bhadrathe,
Bengaluru was examined as RW.3.

Dr.Srinivas Reddy.P, Professor and Head of Department,
Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, Devaraj Urs Medical College, Kolar was examined as RW.4.
The respondent No.2 got examined himself as RW.5.
Ex's .
R5 to 7 were marked through him.

One witness by name Sri.Somashekara S/o Late Chowdaiah was examined on behalf of the respondent No.2 as RW.6.
7.
Oral arguments were addressed on both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows : Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 : The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of the complaint lodged by one Sri. Kishore Kumar (RW.2 herein) the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed chargesheet against the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA05MD9550 (respondent No.1 herein) for the offences punishable under section's 279 & 304(A) of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the chargesheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

During the course of his crossexamination RW.1 (respondent No.1 herein) denied the suggestions that he was driving the car at the time of accident and the deceased died on account of injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that took place due to his negligence.
But he has not challenged the chargesheet that is filed by the jurisdictional police against him.

Thus the unchallenged chargesheet clearly establishes negligence on the part of RW.1.
9.
No doubt respondent No.1 is acquitted in the criminal case registered against him in CC.688/2017 (as per the copy of the judgment which is placed on record by the advocate for respondent No.1).
But in view of the ratio laid down in the decision reported in ILR 2014 KAR 5169 acquittal in a criminal case cannot be the basis to conclude that there was no negligence on the part of the driver.

Moreover it is a settled law that the term 'rashness and negligence' has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act as compared to the word 'rashness and negligence' as finds mention in the IPC.
This is so because the chapter in Motor Vehicles Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

3 10.
The complainant cum eyewitness to the accident in question i.e., RW.2 filed evidence affidavit stating he never lodged any complaint against respondent No.1.
Though he admitted the signature on the complaint to be his signature, he volunteered to state that his signature was obtained on a blank paper by the police.

However this witness could not withstand the test of crossexamination and admitted that :
' I have not filed any complaint stating that my signatures were obtained on a blank paper.
Likewise I have not filed any private complaint before any Court in this regard.
It is true to suggest that I have stated the fact that my signature was obtained on a blank paper by the police before this Court today.

It is true to suggest that as per the say of my advocate I have filed my affidavit. '
11.
In the light of the elicitations extracted supra the testimony of RW.2 cannot be attached any evidentiary value.
Moreso when he has been branded as a 'highly interested witness' by the petitioners.

The reason for such interestedness that can be gathered from the course of cross examination of RW.2 is that he wanted to rescue the respondent No.1 (the actual tortfeasor) who is none other than his brother from the consequences of criminal liability.

Creditworthiness of this witness is further shaken by the fact that he has turned hostile to the case of prosecution in CC.No.688/2017 and deposed contrary to the contents of the very own complaint lodged by him.

Be that as it may, based on the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA05MD9550.
12.
The respondent No.2 examined the investigating officer who investigated crime No.373/2016 of Kolar Rural police station as RW.3.
Anyhow nothing worthwhile would be elicited from his mouth to disbelieve the truthfulness of the investigation carried out by him.
During the course of such examination the counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.2 suggested RW.3 that the deceased was driving the car at the time of accident, which was outrightly denied.
In fact the putting of this suggestion itself goes to show that there is absolutely no merit in the defence taken by the respondent No.2.

This is so because in his written statement the respondent No.2 has taken a specific stand that the respondent No.1 was responsible for causing the accident which is totally divergent to the suggestion put to the investigating officer that the deceased was driving the car at the time of accident.

With this observation, I answer issue No.1 as 'In the Affirmative'.
13. ISSUE NO.2:
The petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of his chiefexamination and deposed that he is the father and petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased.
The documents placed on record reflect the aforesaid relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.

Since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.

Hence they are entitled for compensation under the following heads :
14. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS : Taking into consideration, the age of the deceased as reflected in the Postmortem report i.e., 26 years the appropriate multiplier ) Sri. Ramakrishne Gowda.

M.Y vs ) Sri. Kiran Gowda on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97667870/
4 that would be applicable is '17'.
15.
According to PW.1, the deceased was working as Gym Advisor at Golden Gym and thereby earning an income of Rs.24,000/ p.m.
However neither the avocation and income of the deceased is substantiated by producing cogent materials nor any witness is examined in this regard.

In the absence of proof, taking into consideration the age of the deceased, nature of his work as well as the cost of living, if his notional income is assessed at Rs.8,000/ p.m., it would meet the ends of justice.

In a decision reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd &
others)

others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the Hon'ble Apex Court held that addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in the absence of proof of income.
In the case on hand the deceased was aged 26 years.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SCC 5157, 40% of income is to be added towards future prospects.
40% of Rs.8,000/ works out to Rs.3,200/.
Therefore the total income comes to Rs.11,200/ (8,000 + 3,200).

The deceased was bachelor and as such in view of the proposition of Law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma's case, half of his income needs to be deducted towards personal & living expenses.
1/2 of Rs.11,200/ works out to Rs.5,600/.
Income for consideration is Rs.5,600/ (11,200 - 5,600).
Annual income works out to Rs.67,200/ (5,600 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '17'.

Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.11,42,400/ (67,200 X 17) which is rounded off to Rs.11,43,000/.
16.
LOSS OF CONSORTIUM :

In view of the ratio laid by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Civil Appeal No.2705/2020 between United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Satinder Kaur and others,
each of the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/ on account of loss of consortium and loss of love & affection.

sentences.text: 17. LOSS OF ESTATE: Petitioners are entitled for Rs.15,000/ towards loss of estate.
18. FUNERAL EXPENSES: Petitioners are entitled for Rs.15,000/ towards funeral expenses.

19. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of Dependency : 11,43,00000 2 Loss of Consortium : 80,00000 3 Loss of Estate : 15,00000 4 Funeral Expenses : 15,00000 TOTAL 12,53,00000 20.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
By placing reliance upon the ratio laid down in AIR 2012 SC 100 interest is awarded at the rate of 9% p.a.

Further as the petitioners have established that the accident was caused by the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA05MD9550, the respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the said car (as on the date of accident) is vicariously liable for the act of the driver (respondent No.1).

21. However the specific contention of the respondent No.2 is that on 28.05.2014 he had transferred the ownership of car bearing Reg.No.KA05MD9550 to one Sri.Shaiju for a sum of Rs.90,000/.
Subsequent to such transfer of ownership and delivery of car to Shaiju he was under the bonafide )

5 belief that said Shaiju would have got changed the RC of the car to his name.
But as manifest from the police records and the evidence of RW.3, as on the date of accident the RC of the car bearing Reg.No.KA05MD9550 stood in the name of respondent No.2.

Moreover during the course of his crossexamination RW.5 himself admitted suggestions to the effect that : ' It is true to suggest that car bearing Reg.No.KA05MD9550 was standing in my name as on the date of accident.
It is true to suggest that even one year after the occurrence of the accident, the RC was continuing in my name.

It is true to suggest that I do not possess any documents to show that I have sold my car to one Mr. Shaiju ', which make it amply clear that respondent No.2 was the RC owner of the offending car at the time of accident.

22. It is relevant to note that as per Sec.2(30) of the MV Act it is the person in whose name the motor vehicle stands registered, would be treated as owner of the vehicle for the purposes of the said act.

In the case of Naveen Kumar V/s Vijay Kumar and others reported in (2018) 3 SCC 1, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that 'In view of the definition of the expression 'owner' in Section 2(30)
of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988, it is the person in whose name the motor vehicle stands registered,
who, for the purposes of the said act, would be treated as owner of the vehicle.

entities.text: Naveen Kumar V/s Vijay Kumar and others reported in (2018) 3 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Where the registered owner purports to transfer the vehicle but continues to be reflected in the records of the Registering Authority as the owner of the vehicle, he would not stand absolved of his liability as owner'.
(Emphasis supplied).

23. Hence by placing reliance upon the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in the decision cited supra,
I hold that the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest thereon @ 9% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
24. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.12,53,000/ (Rupees Twelve Lakhs Fifty Three Thousand only) with interest at the rate of 9% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1  50%
 Petitioner No.2  50%
